text: I could say a lot of things, but I'll just say this... if you really want to go here for service, make sure you have a ride and drop your car off. If you make an afternoon appointment, don't be surprised if they cancel from overbooking. If you try to call them when they open, don't be surprised if the phone goes unanswered.  If you're told to just come in around lunch for an inspection, don't.  Everyone leaves around lunch. If you ask for more than one service to be done on your car, expect something to be forgotten and check before leaving that all work was done. If you choose to wait on your vehicle, expect to wait several hours. If you have the shop order tires for you, anticipate they might not get there by your appointment date. Most of all, prices are much higher than their competition  here, chaos is ever-present, and I really can't put together how busy they are for how many appointment or scheduling  issues, promises broken, and other issues I witnessed in addition to my own while waiting over 2 hours... I don't blame the techs at all. The issue seems to be isolated to mostly the front end.

text: This place is incredible! They were super nice & helpful. My client (eldery lady)needed help with the tire on her motorized scooter. We drove to store, purchased tube & came back. Country roads then put everything back together..FREE OF CHARGE! Im not saying they do all kinds of things for free but the fact that they were willing to help an elderly woman fix her only mode of transportation for free is incredibly nice! Everyone we encountered there was friendly, helpful & had a smile on their face. I would 100% recommend this place 10000000 times over & over to anyone

text: One of my favorite places in West Virginia. Great skiing!

name: Granville Senters
text:
This place is beautiful. There is a lot to do. And so much potential!!! But there are some convenience issues especially anywhere outside The Village itself. Very little choices in the way of groceries and stores period. There is absolutely no cell signal anywhere outside The Village. Internet anywhere outside The Village is satellite internet which picks and chooses when it wants to work and how slow it wants to work. Plus everything everywhere is overpriced massively, especially groceries, and because of the lack of options within an hour's drive there is no choice but to pay it.
Honestly with some modern development in the surrounding area with the addition of improvements to all the surrounding areas infrastructure this area could become the "Gatlinburg/Pigeon Forge" of West Virginia.

name: Robin Fisher
text:
The mountain is like a ghost town. SO ENJOYABLE! Beautiful blue sky against the mountain range, breath taking.
No restaurant nor shopping is open,bring all of  your groceries you will need or else it is a long drive to the nearest IGA. Pocahontas IGA was awesome, had everything we needed at great prices.

name: WV Almost Heaven
text:
Your friends & family may beg you to go to Snowshoe Mountain Resort. They'll say, "you'll enjoy the scenery", "we'll enjoy a meal together", "we know you can't ski, but there will be shopping and plenty of things to do beside ski". Not If you're handicapped there won't be! Most of the shops, or at least the several that I saw, are not handicap accessible.

In "the village" if you think there is handicapped parking, NOPE. The 5 *FIVE* 5 slots (yes only 5) handicap parking spots they have, will be filled with non-handicapped employees and/or business owners, none of which will have handicap license plates (as I do) nor handicap placards. In fact on this occassion a business called Hospitality Services occupied one slot ALL DAY! So much for hospitality.

Do not make the mistake of asking folks who work there to point out the handicap accessibilities. They will give you a blank stare and then shrug their shoulders and say, "Gee I don't think there are any"(true story). The entire facility is anti-handicap. There are stairs everywhere, no ramps. All buildings are locked up tight, denying access to elevators. If any handicap features do exist, the 7 people employed there that I asked didn't know of any.

If you are physically handicapped you have 3 choices. 1) drop your friends or family off and then drive down the mountain and wait at a gas station, 2) sit in your vehicle in some remote/removed parking lot & burn your vehicles fuel or 3) (another true story) let your friends and family carry you like some Egyptian Pharaoh !UP! to a  business, which will then ask you to leave 2 hours hours after your last purchase; because there are physically abled patrons who want your seat (who will only occupy it for 30 minutes or less, because they have skiing to do). But your friends and family are SKIING too and cannot relocate you. They make an exception just this once, as if you will ever be back, fat chance!

At Snowshoe you ARE NOT welcomed if you are handicapped! Even if you were welcomed, Snowshoe is inaccessible to physically handicapped people. Stay home and let your friends & family go spend a day without you. Unless of course you want to be mocked and/or berated by the MOBILITY ELITE.

Note: There may be those of you, who in your minds might say "You're handicapped, you shouldn't be there in the first place." It is easy to say that in your mind. What would you think if you heard someone say that out loud to a handicapped person? You may be one of those that would think that if someone said it out loud to a handicapped person they would be wrong to do so. Thinking it is just as wrong. Yes, I was told that I shouldn't be there by someone who worked there.

text: We had a wonderful time at snowshoe. The weather in our hometown was in the mid-90's, but it was 70 at snowshoe. Believe it or not, I had a light jacket on in the early mornings. They also just paved the road up the mountain which is nice.

name: JM Bauer
text:
We stayed just before Xmas 2019. The staff at the resort are courteous and get the job done. We were able to get checked in in no time.

The skiing was okay. There are long and challenging runs on the Western Territory, and decent night skiing at Silver Creek. Unfortunately the green runs tended to be crowded and long lift lines were an issue after 10:00 AM. The resort did a great job of keeping the runs open in spite of the relatively mild weather. It is unfortunate that no ski runs connect the main  area and Silver Creek.

The place can feel crowded and perhaps a little lacking in atmosphere. The old timers one meets around the resort spin great stories about the mountain. Snowshoe could better share these stories and more about West Virginia with its guests.

name: Brandon Drake
text:
Take a yearly trip here, for the last 12 years. It is unique to have mountain top lodging, restaurants, etc. Most places are ski in/ski out. The Junction restaurant is our favorite but there are several on the mountain. The village is such an awesome setting, to walk through and shop. Its rarely over crowded here as well and lift lines are usually short, except.for Saturdays and holidays, it can be packed.
Also, pro tip, Top of the World for lodging, easy access with free parking, best prices on the mountain and ski in,/ski out at the top of widowmaker slope. There are green trails leading to and from as well. There is terrain here for every skill type, nice terrain parks, gentle to extreme slopes at the western territory, and great fast lifts as well. Highly recommend over any other resort in WV, been to them all.

The food all looked fresh with healthy portions.  I had the steak & cheese, which was still bigger than i could eat tho smaller than some places.  I had the hummus, too, which was tasty.

Service was prompt & friendly.  I had to park a couple blocks away tho by the time i walked there a couple spaces opened up.  They have 5 or 6 spots right in front.

Really fun place for a road trip.  There are lots of adorable, unique shops in town, too, and a boat ramp with potomac river access is a few blocks away with some small falls.  The same stream, i assume.

text: Blue Moon is a college town hipster Pub that serves overpriced food.  The atmosphere is very pleasant aesthetically (especially the outdoor area) but good luck getting a seat.  Regulars fill the area and then spend a very long time at the tables.  They do have a lot of vegetarian, vegan, and gluten free options, but again, for what you get it is always expensive.  The service is normally (4/5 visits) slow and inattentive and if you ask a question or want something done special expect a college student eye roll.  This is a restaurant you will only find in a college town and if you can stand the apathetic staff, snooty clientele, and don't care about the cost to value it might be somewhere you want to eat, drink, and enjoy the ambiance.

name: Michael Mastrianni
text:
Perfect for singles, couples or groups alike, the atmosphere at Blue Moon Cafe is incredible. When you first walk in, you are greeted by someone in the restaurant and it's a very welcoming place. Blue Moon offers both indoor and outdoor seating and if outdoor seating is available, they ask if you prefer it. As a Shepherd University student, Blue Moon is very close to campus and is easily accessible for any Shepherd student. During the summer months, Blue Moon is a popular spot and thus you might have to make a reservation. In my 3 years at Shepherd University, Blue Moon is at the top of my food preferences in town.

As for the food, it's hard to not find a food option I wouldn't be interested in trying. As someone with a restricted diet, Blue Moon has plenty of options still for me. My top picks would be the crab melts for an appetizer and the chubby burger for the meal.

All in all, Blue Moon is an easy-going, well located restaurant in a cozy historic town that offers some of the best food available, and is a must for anyone in Shepherdstown. Students, residents of Shepherdstown, tourists and those just driving through will find Blue Moon a must to visit.

text: We arrived, were seating promptly, and had our order taken (rather rudely). I ordered a crab cake sandwich with chips, and my friend ordered a steak and cheese sub with fries; nothing too fancy, right? Our food arrived almost an hour later. By that time, my friend had to ask for a to-go box when the waitress brought our food because she had to leave. Our waitress was rude. Upon paying, we were instructed to go to the register. We did, and, since my friend was in a hurry (and there were several workers standing around behind the register), she politely asked the woman behind the register if she could go ahead and pay the bill because she was in a hurry. The woman then proceeded to put her finger up in my friend's face and answer the telephone, and instead of asking the person if they could hold, she turned her back to my friend and began talking to the person on the telephone. The food we ordered was good, but nothing spectacular. I had heard good things about this place, but a lot of those "good things" had "...but the staff aren't the nicest," added at the end. We will not be going back, and will be letting others know of our experience.

Cashing out at the front I'd say the cashier was acting as though she'd worked the busiest 14 hour shift at a New York restaurant... but it was WV, and it was 5:00pm... Grouchy, worn out, borderline rude... but at least I only had to associate with her for a few seconds..

Overall though, I'd say it was pretty good.. I'd go back a few more times for the food and the atmosphere. If the service remained the same everytime, I'd go somewhere else. Everyone has a bad/off day... I wouldn't knock them off completely for that.

The work was completed in good time. We were satisfied enough to bring another Ford for service.  This needed more than the first and while there I asked about a windshield since mine had been damaged by a rock thrown from a trailer months before. What I appreciated was that I was told that they do not have a shop to sell the windshield but they had a relationship with a local glass service and that the glass service would fix my windshield on Parson's property.

This may not seem like a big deal but it was nice to see a willingness on the part of a dealer service department to (in my opinion) go a little further to make sure I was happy with the end result.

We finally feel like we have found a dealer we can trust with our car repairs.

So, if you need Ford service, please look into the service department at Kent Parson's Ford.

My mustang has had issues since day one. I have now had it two years and only one issue had been fixed which was the ambient lighting. The program would not hold.

I have numerous videos of the issue and dealerships response is bring it by when it acts up.

Door mirrors over extend themselves and grind and click. The first time I showed service writer the video he said and I quote "close the door. It's trying to find the rear wheel. It's supposed to do that"

So I took multiple videos of both driver's side and passenger side clicking at different times with the doors closed. They do this maybe every 25 times the door is opened. They kept the car over a week and ordered wrong parts.

The car is now out of bumper to bumper warranty. So I don't know if I'm going to be stuck with this until the mirrors completely break.

The other issue is the sync system. It locks up constantly, and also says USB hub not supported. With nothing plugged in it still says the same thing. The hub is the Port itself not the device.

The odd thing is... When sync acts up so do the mirrors.

Since they keep emailing me bugging me to leave them a review of my experience regarding my brand new vehicle purchase, I figure I might as well oblige.

This was my first new car,as well as my first custom order, and my experience from both FoMoCo and Parson's Ford was abhorrent!

The salesman that I was sent to didn't know much at all about the vehicle I wanted to buy, he did not know anything about the custom factory options, and he had terrible communication skills.

He went and ordered the vehicle and that was it. Three months of checking in later and we had no answers.

The estimated delivery date came and went, still no word from Ford, no word from the salesman, nothing.

I call oneday and find out from the operator that my salesman was no longer there, and nobody was given my file!

Nobody had any idea what was going on!

So I spoke to the sales manager and while he didn't do anything in particular to help, he was at least cool about it all and helped keep me in the loop until it came in. Which was really all that I expected.

In the end, I got the van, but boy was it a fight to get them to simply do what I would have expected to have been a simple vehicle order.

*UPDATE* I have since purchased two more new vehicles from Parson's, and have had much better results. I will adjust my review accordingly, but if you are looking for a no BS sales experience, I highly recommend speaking to Brett Wright!

He, and he alone is the reason that I have continued to return and even give Parson's another chance. I really enjoy working with a straight shooter that is not afraid to give me the pro's and con's right up front, someone who tells me exactly what he can and cannot do to make a sale. No haggling, no "let me ask my manager", just "Here's the price, here's what we can do it for, and here's these rebates/discounts.".

resp.text: We are very saddened to hear about this. I want to apologize again for the miscommunications. I can guarantee we have the same sales managers we had all year of 2018 if that helps? Please reach out to Ryan Byrd at 3042633344 ext 103 and  allow him to help.

name: Jodie Greenfield
text:
I have to say I never thought I'd rate this place so poorly.  I'll start off with my father in law has purchased 7 or 8 brand new Fords from Kent Parsons  (Ryan Byrd) over the last 21 years.  My hub has always wanted me to drive a Ford but I'm a Lexus gal.  About 8 or 9 months ago my daughter wanted to purchase her first car on her own (Ford)and my husband was adamant that we only use Ryan.  It just so happened  that at first we went to Hagerstown due to Parsons being closed on Sundays.  So in Hagerstown we worked an entire deal as if we were buying. I must say it was a killer deal.  My hub had a fit however and talked my daughter in to waiting til Monday and only buying from Ryan.  Well long story short that was not his smartest decision.  My daughter not only left the dealer,   broke down , (in a brand new 2017 Focus , This was her sign ) but,  left with not the right insurance (full coverage) only to find out later and up adding over 3k a year making her payment with Patriot go up from $440 to $728 a month ...its dealers responsibility to make sure car fully covered (he did apologize later and say dont know how I missed that ) what  Ryan did do WAS SELL HER GAP INSURANCE, mind you Gap left us sit along side of road a few days ago for three hrs with blown out tire , cost $40 a month, this isnt the worst of it.  My daughter bought a 2017 Ford Focus.  She traded in a 2014 Jeep Patouit ...she was upside down 4k.  But Ryan told her with incentives on the Focus it would cover it .. NOT HARDLY! ...by the time my daughter left she FINANCED $31K FOR A $22k dollar car.   When they got home and I looked over paper work I immediately called and was CALM AND COOL thinking this was a mistake , never thinking Ryan would screw such GOOD CUSTOMERS OVER.  I WAS WRONG.  Ryan avoided me. Never returned messages or calls.. so my husband just knew this was a mistake too and went back.  IT WASNT.  RYAN actually told my hub the best thing my daughter could do is wear a helmet and total the car TO GET OUT OF IT...I am applauded.  To end this I had published a Local Magazine .  Ryan and his boss both said during the purchase of her car they would put an ad in the magazine it was the least they could do considering ALLLLL THE BUSINESS my Family gave them.  They dodged me during 3 trips to Parsons and they had invited me there and they would not even meet with me less alone run a ad..  I so wish this weren't true.  But it is.  The last thing is I do know this loan SHOULD NOT BE VALID. considering my father in law was the co signer who didnt sign Because he was in Keyser that day.   So , I guess we need to check into this.

Next id like to respond to who ever responded to this review and say I did call and email like you advised and Ryan Has Not Returned Calls or Emails ! So while its a great gesture to look like like a business who  cares its even more more heartbreaking to a loyal client.

text: This place is surprisingly really good. We've lived here since 2011 and just tried this location this year. We've had bad experiences with another location. But I don't judge a restaurant on its food, I judge it on the service. The service here is amazing. We had one server who was having a bad day and therefore wasn't up to par, but everyone else has been top notch. If you're looking for typical food but amazing service Ruby Tuesday is the place.

text:
My cheeseburger tasted and smelled like fish. My husband and I had the takeout option, by the time we got home it was too far away to take it back. I called the restaurant, and was told that the hamburger was probably cooked on the same side as where they grill the salmon. Let me repeat that, the grill the hamburger on the same side as they grilled the fish. there is absolutely no common sense and realizing that the two flavors would bleed onto each other.

As with all takeout and restaurants nowadays there's there is a lack of empathy for a situation such as mine.I understand the call was undoubtedly unusual for the young lady, however, when disconnect the call I was not left with the impression that the kitchen would be alerted, or the manager would be told
to enforce the fact that you do not cook hamburger on the same side as fish.

It has been a while since I have worked in the fast-food industry, but I do seem to remember there were some health issue violations that raw hamburger and fish are not to be done on the same grill. We  will eat at Ruby Tuesday's again as we do generally have a pleasant experience however, again we will not ever do the you take out option because the kitchen usesxuses thisathis astas an excuse to not make food correctly. We have no recourse by the time the customer gets home.

text:
Ruby Tuesday is a lot like your typical chain in many ways and I was expecting as much. I was pleasantly surprised today by how well our dishes were prepared today. Both my father and I ordered the Tilapia and I was amazed at how perfectly the fish was cooked.

I typically expect fish at restaurants like these to be on the overcooked side and dry. Today the fish was cooked just perfectly -- it was moist and flaky exactly the way tilapia ought to be!

I don't normally review chain restaurants like this but seeing the other relatively negative reviews I wanted to note that the service was great, the food was very well prepared and that the other reviews may not have been fair.

If you're looking for something consistent with slightly higher quality than you're typical chain restaurant, this Ruby Tuesday is a good choice.

text: The curly headed young man who is managing right now as I write this review is working an impossible situation and is handling himself very well. He is extremely short staffed, he is out of the number one thing that people are coming to this restaurant for (Chicken Sandwiches), he is out of Barbeque sauce, and he is out of nearly all of his coke products. Yet, I have personally watched him (unbeknownst to him) single handedly run the drive thru, work the kitchen, replenish exhausted food, take orders, call what he needs dropped, run food out to waiting customers and assist his slower cashier that he had working.  This young man worked circles around 3 other staffers in an effort to keep the restaurant's customers happy. My order was incomplete and (I Never received  my fish that was ordered) knew that the young man who was working himself crazy did not give me my order as advised; I checked in with him at the register. The young man's register was giving him issues and as I patiently waited while he worked frantically tried to work through his issues at the register, I advised the young man..."instead of fish, how about some boneless chicken?" The very relieved young man gladly took care of my order and all was well. To this young man's managers...you have a very customer obsessed, results driven young man running your restaurant at the time of this review... Make sure that you do right by him! Great job young man!!!

text: Do NOT book a birthday party here. We only received one 12" inch pizza and one pitcher of soda for our party. We were told there were no other pizzas so we couldn't even order any more. So the guests decided hot dogs would suffice but guess what? No hot dogs. So I ordered 7 small fries and a steak and cheese sub for $40.  The food took nearly 45 minutes to make and we didn't get to eat until an hour into the party. By the time we finished eating and opening presents, our 2 hour were up so no one got to bowl. Try explaining that to a disappointed 6 year old little girl who had been looking forward to her party for weeks.  All told, I got a room for 2 hours, one 12" cheese pizza, one pitcher of soda, 7 fries, and 1 sub for $125. I wouldn't care if this was the last bowling alley on the planet - I will NEVER step foot there ever again.

When I called, I got apparently the biggest dud at comcast, who advised me a technician would be out the following day between 1 and 3. No one showed, I called in and they verified I was lied to. Next appointment September 5. I said no, we can cancel. Get sent to customer service, they want to check for an earlier date, September 4. I said no, we are done here. I appear to not be the only one with issues, as they are rated poorly. I see why. text: I ordered a rosette cake. Meaning the whole cake would be covered in roses. She looked as confused as I was and got deli/bakery manager. The manager then tells me I ordered wrong. (I make cakes myself, so I assure you I did not) however the girl that took the order seemed new and confused. I had to explain to her what butter cream icing was and also explain 3 different times their would be no icing showing. Just the rosettes. She said if they had any questions they would call. Never did I receive one call and when I spoke with the manager by the name of Valerie who then told me ,I messed up not them and those were roses. "Rose's without petals " were her exact words. I finally spoke to a manager of the store after Valerie refused to get one. The actual manager went above and beyond to try and make it right. (Ray sullivan) That did not stop my disappointed 4yo from saying "well for my next birthday can I have my blue cake". The store as a whole is great. But stay away from the deli and bakery or you will end up ordering a cake that was made by a 5yo. The icing was literaly falling off the sides as well as blank holes throughout. So let's say it was covered in "roses without petals" lol why are their gaping holes and icing sliding off the cake? I personally would not want a manager who curses at customers and walks away refusing to fix their own mistakes running any part of my store.  An for the rest of the bakery employees who laughed in my face as the store manager cursed at me and walked away leaving me with no cake and refusing to allow me to see the order form to prove it was not my mistake. I hope you all have the same experience on your child's birthday.

name: Stephanie Morris
text:
The staff in the hotel is very welcoming.  They kept the rooms very clean and stocked each day we were here. There are not a lot of "perks" at this hotel, but perhaps that is understandable in the chain. Location is fantastic for views, but the area is sketchy if you are going to be out late in the evening or night.   We witnessed several would be drug deals going on across the street with plastic bag drops that were later picked up by backpackers. Not a safe feeling and that leads me to my next point.
My one complaint, as a smoker, ( I understand, this makes most uncomfortable) they did not have a designated area for someone to go out and smoke.  The garage parking would have been fine with us in the open air areas with receptacles.  Instead we were required to go to the edge of Kanawha Blvd on the sidewalk to smoke and bring our butts back to the trash can outside the front of the hotel.  I am just used to going to hotels that have designated areas that are actually safe to the clientele, I suppose.

name: Clark Zealand
text:
The Four Points by Sheraton Charleston is a very nice hotel. We chose this property mainly because of the location to appointments however; the hotel is a great location, for not only business but the guest rooms as well. The hotel has many great amenities including conference rooms, business center, lobby bar, lobby restaurant, heated indoor pool, and workout room. Onsite parking is adequate but at least you do not have to pay extra. Location is central to many places in Charleston and serves as a great place from which to travel and see the sights as well.
The following are the main observations during our stay:
1.	Room was a nice size with good window views
2.	Queen size beds have comfortable mattresses and pillows
3.	Rooms clean and up to date and cleaning staff did a great job
4.	Bathroom was clean with plenty of hot water
5.	Hotel interior is very unique with all hallways clean as well
6.	Restaurant food is quite good for a hotel and staff are very friendly
7.	Hotel amenities are clearly kept up to date and in good conditions
If you are looking for a nice hotel or if you are attending for a conference, you will not be disappointed.

Tonight's stay has been atrocious and stressful start to finish and the only shining light was the woman who works the bar in the evening.

text:
Stayed at this location on the evening of March 15 with my wife and 2 year old son whom was having surgery the next morning.  The older lady that checked us in seemed confused?  Only word I can think of to use.  She tells me to insert my credit card into the machine and I had to ask her to confirm what I will be charged.  She confirms the room rate and then after I sign and she gives me the keys that "oh, and parking is $10 it'll be on your card" .  This was 1st problem as I hadn't been told this when reserving.  We then get up to the 10th floor room, open the door with the key, and find someone else's belongings on one of the beds.  We go back downstairs and are given a different room with not much of an apology from the older lady.  After settling in, I go down to get a cocktail for my wife and I.  The person working the bar had no clue how to make the drinks I ordered (cosmopolitan & long island) and had to ask another employee passing by to look it up on his cell phone.  After waiting for them to be made, I'm told "that'll be $28!!!"
The drinks were absolutely disgusting.  I complained to corporate via phone the next day and they advised the hotel would have 5 days to respond to me.  The hotel did not make any attempt to contact me, and corporate thankfully has agreed to refund me in full for my troubles.  This is the only reason I have given 1 star. name: Ashon Woodbury
text:
Chick-fil-A is always a great addition to everyone's day. From the service to the food, you can't go wrong here. There are many menu items to choose from and just as many sauces to pair with them. Chick-fil-A sauce is worth it every time!

The lemonade is made on-site, which makes it one of the best lemonades you will have; especially in the West Virginia summer! If you want something with less sugar, the diet lemonade option is a great one. All of the taste with less sugar. I have never had a bad experience here.

Then there is breakfast, which is better than any other fast food experience. The chicken minis alone are worth the trip. If you have not had these, stop reading and try them now! The drive thru is handled very well. When busy, the staff takes your order on mobile, so you will not have to wait very long until your order is ready.

The restaurant is easy to enter and exit in the plaza, which is a plus!

Download the app to get even more rewards and discounts including free food at times. If you eat here, the app is an absolute must every time!

text:
I want to be fair to the CTC of today and refrain from comparing it to the CTC of the past. Today's CTC still has friendly associates in the various stores, still has a fair parking garage ($1 75 for all day or metered parking available) and is clean and tidy. Security was present and welcoming, the food court has a decent variety of choices and there is still one remaining anchor store, JC Penney,

There is a decent variety of small shops on the two floors, but there are so many empty spaces and a feeling of emptiness in general. I was there at lunch time yet it was so empty of shoppers that many associates were outside the business simply for lack of anything better to do.

The CTC heyday is long past, I'm afraid. Still, it was a good day with my daughter, who is too young to know it any other way.

text:
This is the only choice for up to the minute styles in one convenient location, honestly, for clothes and shoes for hard to shop for teenage kids or high maintenance people with a taste for higher end brand names..If you are the spare no expense on what you want or savvy in the new and now, or simply a regular teen or tween that wears what is typically in style with higher priced name brands. I personally dont spend more than I have to on anything, and I readily admit to the weakness of spoiling our 4 kids-- BUT I also try to teach that clothes are only as good as the person wearing them, and a great attitude can wear anything if you have confidence! But, without being naive, I know how mean other kids can be in judging by monetary value,and the ignorance adults can instill on their impressionable minds, so I try to point out what others seem to be wearing and find acceptable as "in style", but make it a point to teach appreciation to those providing for their needs.
You can catch sales on many instances, but I feel it is more often the case, too high for many items as this is the only choice, unless you shop online, to get any choice of styles and certain brands not found anywhere else. It is our only mall for at least 60+ miles or more, so we really have little choice in where to go clothes or tech shopping.Shoes is an obvious reason, as no other places have the brands or selection that the different stores in the Town Center has.

text:
This park is not particularly scenic, but it’s a good place to take a long walk. The trail provides opportunities for a level stroll around a lake, or an energetic climb up a steep hill to a network of trails on the top. There are no signs, and there is no trail map. You simply wander the interconnecting trails until you decide to make your way back down the hill.

There are two sets of trails. Well-established wide trails cut through the property in a sort of grid, and newer narrow trails wind through the trees in a long loop that intersects the wide trails at several points. It sounds like a recipe for getting lost, but all trails eventually lead back to the trailhead at the bottom of the hill. The park’s website gives the total mileage as 5.1.

A disc golf course was added to the trail system several years ago, and it is well used. You might think that this use would conflict with hiking, but the disc golfers I've met have been friendly and didn't seem to think I was intruding. If you are concerned about getting lost on the trails, you could follow the disc golf course.

The newer trails were built for mountain biking, but I've never seen anyone on a bike there.  They do get a fair amount of use from disc golfers and people walking for exercise.

The woods are a typical oak-hickory forest.  Poison ivy abounds, so watch what you touch. You’ll also see lots of invasive plants like Tartarian honeysuckle and autumn olive. One of the invasives, a red raspberry locally known as wine berries, produces fruit in July, and picking is permitted. The tart, waxy fruit is good fresh and in pies.

Wildlife consists mostly of songbirds. The lake, which is stocked with game fish, has ducks and some Canada geese. Watch your step if you take the trail around the lake. There is a cattail marsh north of the lake, where I've heard spring peepers and red-winged blackbirds.

If you don’t have time to drive to amazing hiking spots like Antietam Battlefield or Shenandoah National Park, this is a good place to stretch your legs.

name: Lynda Fowler
text:
This is our usual place to grab dinner once a week, at the same time. There seems to be new employees working every time we stop in.
I really can't say much for the food, I'll only get chips and queso, sometimes a quesadilla, but if the queso sauce is almost empty and what's left is the dark, crusty, skin-topped with whatever has fallen into the sauce over it's time out, is all that's left, I will always ask for fresh queso. This will almost always be met with looks of exasperation and subtle eye-rolling because I'm holding up the line.
That being said, it's hit or miss. Since its always the same day at the same time, maybe that's when the line workers are at the end of their shifts and just want to leave. My kids enjoy the food and you can go as healthy or filthy as you want with your order, plenty of options.
One HUGE peeve, if you try to order online, you can only order certain menu items. If you want quesadillas added or anything that's not a burrito, it can't be ordered online.

text: How can you not love it! Never had issues OF ANY KIND EVER! And I have been a loyal customer since it first opened in Frederick before it even came to Hagerstown or Martinsburg or anywhere else out here!!!! Yet never had issues at others even when its a busy time. It is always good food. HOWEVER; ITS THE SERVICE, YOURE MARTINSBURG LOCATION IS AWFUL. no matter the time of day, there are always people waiting, at least 10 for their food whether its online order or whatever like doordash. The last 3 times I have ordered from the app and still get that 15 min or so time frame but get there and are still waiting 20-45 minutes for food. It is always now an hour to hour and a half for an order from here which is just ludacris! Get more people in there to work or make the app smarter to adjust to real actual wait times.

text: I enjoy Chipotle alot when I get to go.  The food is made right in front of you and they have a well order system so that you get your food fast.  I normally wait to eat there when they are having a sale or promotion due to price.  The food is good quality but can be a little pricey for a burrito.  I have only ever had one issue at Chipotle which was an employee who clearly had not done a good job wrapping the burrito and it was leaking badly before they foiled it up.  The bad thing is that in order to have gotten it fixed I would have had to hold up the line and have them reopen and then rewrap the burrito.  I chose to just take it "as is" and not mention it to anyone but it was really disappointing to have to wait until I got somewhere that I could deconstruct the burrito before I could eat.  Other than that all of my experiences have been good and I will frequent Chipotle in the future.

text: The vegan Gardein wings were good, but nothing I couldn’t have microwaved at home. Only two of the sauce options are vegan (Mild and BBQ). The salad had to be modified, so we ended up with apple shreds and not much else. I’d recommend adding some more plant-based toppings like avocado, beans, tofu, or just more veggies if someone cannot have meat or cheese. Service was excellent and open to modifications!

resp.text:
Hello Christina,

Thank you for the review. We are happy to be one of the only sports grills to offer a vegan wing option. We are sorry this option did not knock it out of the park for you. We are always happy to modify and meet the special needs of any diet. We appreciate the feedback, as we are always looking to improve our menu options. We hope to see you again soon!

RSG

text: A few decent beers, friendly, outside dining is as dull as the nearby sidewalk, but better than being bombarded by the many TV's inside.  BUT - Got the ribs and they were so underdone and tough they were seriously inedible. Like "gum cutting stringy" tough.  They appeared to compensate for this by drowning them in sauce, which never works, and made most of the fries soggy.  Reluctantly tried again a year later,  told server about the ribs last time and was assured it must have been a glitch, but ribs again came way underdone and too tough to eat.  To be fair, the TV assault alone is just not my thing, If that's your thing go for it. But after it all, two stars for friendly beers.

text: Super disappointed. The last three times we've come for dinner the food has been great but the service has been soooo slow! We only ordered wings and 2 grilled cheese so it shouldnt have taken so long! It's now 7:15 and we are finally leaving, the only reason the waitress came back to our table is because she saw us gathering our stuff up.

text:
The food served was OK.  Nothing spectacular, but good nonetheless. The service for the restaurant is not exactly the best. You feel like you are putting someone out to attend to your table.
The bar seating and bar tenders are excellent, however.  Our first night there it was Britney S. and she was so accommodating and attentive to us!

resp.text: Thanks for sharing your feedback, Stephanie! We always appreciate detailed feedback such as this and will definitely share it with our management team in attempt to workout some of the kinks. We are happy to hear about your overall experience and hope to see you again soon!

text:
Great sports bar with a HUGE set of TVs, so any game you want will probably be on. Add to that, the personal speakers at each table allow you to select the audio for the game you want.

For food and drink, there's a great selection of craft beer on tap (Devil Anse IPA FTW!) and tasty bar food.

Seriously, if you don't have a great man cave at home, this is a great option.

The did not bring an order of fries, and my wings certainly weren't roasted, but we just paid and left. Didn't have time for them to fix it. The atmosphere is nice and other reviews are good. I'll probably give it another shot sometime, but only because others have given it good reviews.

Hello James,

RSG

Would recommend to anyone looking for good food.

text: This is a very nice and large sports bar that is well maintained. It wasn't very crowded when we arrived however the service at the bar was still slow. The margarita was nice and refreshing on a hot day. The chicken tacos were so dry they were they hard to eat. Most likely pre-made chicken that was reheated to long? The draft beer I ordered had a layer of soapy ice float to the top which I couldn't drink. Probably the glass wasn't rinsed and dried properly before being frosted?  All places have a off day or period at times so I'll return in the future to give it another go.

Great for watching games with the family or friends while having a good snack or some beer.

name: ROBERT CALDERONE
text:
Great place to live and raise a family if you have one.
99% of homeowners maintain their homes and manicure their landscaping to perfection.
Crime and vandalism is practically non-existent because the residents respect each other and their properties.
Very quiet & somewhat dark at night as it should be.
Subdivision was planned to have a country feel & look to it and it does.
That's the reason the old section has no sidewalks curbs or street lights and we don't want them.
If you need those things then you don't like rural country living.
Of the few aggravations are all the speed bumps to slow people down and prevent them from running stop signs.
The new section was built to cater to commuters and has more amenities and smaller yards that people from big cities are used to.
We also have a beautiful large swimming pool and tennis courts which is included in your association fees.

text: Unfortunately, our trip to this establishment left us very sick. I first visited this establishment when it opened in 2016. The food was made hot and fresh to your specifications of how you wanted it done. It was very on point. The service from the staff was phenomenal.  Fast forward two years. The food that we ordered was not fresh nor hot. Nor was the coffee or the hot water that your supposed to get when you order hot tea. We sat at the table for almost ten minutes before someone took our order. The young ladies that were at the register were too busy talking, taking smoke breaks, and paying  attention to the white people while ignoring us the black people. The food that we ordered was overcooked and dry. Portions of it was so hard that it seemed as if, it had been sitting under a heat lamp or left in a pot with the top off drying out.  It was so hard that I couldn't even use my fork on it to break it up. Other portions were undercooked. I couldn't find a manager to speak with about the customer service, which I later found out that he could not take care of the front of the house, due to him being in the kitchen cooking. What made it worse, was that the Management was cooking and allowed this type of food to be sent out to a customer, that is not professional. I understand that sometimes businesses will be understaffed, but that's no excuse for proper service. You should never send subpar food out to your customers to consume. There should always be a manager to take care of any customer concern. No matter what, there should not be any exceptions. I will not be giving this establishment any more of my business. If, I could give a negative review that would give them no star, I would.

text:
Me and some friends went there on Christmas Eve and our experience was amazing. Our server was fantastic and service was exemplary. I typically drink a lot when I go to places and it was absolutely the case this time. I had several refills during my time and our waiter even made jokes about it, but he was both professional and nice about it even offering me though I declined on it.

The restaurant was both clean and had a really nice look about it and felt really homely. IHOPs menu contains both a good variety of diner food and Breakfast items. More than likely you can find something you like. I had a Turkey Wrap with a side salad, in which the waiter made a hilarious joke about and our table loved it. The price of the items are really fair and the food is both tasty and filling. The avocados that were in my wrap were originally going to be my concern, but they were surprisingly fresh considering it's late December and they are out of season. My salad was also really fresh and had a good mixture of toppings. To my disappointment they do not have any lite dressings for the salad, but it was still good.

By far the worst service I've had at a restaurant. I'm sure that our occasion may have only been this way because of a poorly equipped and under qualified staff, but that is not excuse for the poor attitude of the server that we had to ask literally 13 times for one orange juice that he "kept forgetting". Of the five of us that were there, two of us had the correct drinks and food without having to ask 4-5 times for the one we'd ordered the first time. The manager was clearly overloaded that day, poor girl, and was very apologetic towards our humorous dissatisfaction. We weren't rude, every time they'd mess up we'd just laugh it off. No point in reaming someone publicly and making a scene.

Needless to say I will not be back for a long while because of our bad experience and incorrect food, that we paid for anyways.

name: Noah Basden
text: The great thing about this IHOP is how close it is to the hospital. I cat eat as fast as I please and if a fat stack of pancakes becomes lodged in windpipe, I can whimsically gasp for life-giving air, knowing that a medical doctor is just an ihop and a skip away. The doctor can remove the pancakes from my trachea with some tongs. She will smile at me, looking at me, then looking at the tongs holding the pancakes that were moments ago killing me. She bites the soggy pancakes and says "mmmm blueberry syrup." I fall in love but leave brokenhearted knowing that a medical doctor could never love a man who chokes on pancakes, even though we both love blueberry syrup. Pancakes are love.  My waitress smelled my armpits and told me they "smelled fine".

name: Joy Seeker
text: This historical small town has done a great job of keeping it to it's original state.  We parked our car at the Harper's Ferry Visitor Center, and took their free shuttle service to the town.  There is very limited parking around the town itself, but plenty of parking at the Visitors Center.  The museums depict the time of the civil war.The town is small enough to walk through so comfortable footwear with good traction due to the cobblestone streets and steep hills to climb. Atop a hill you will view an old railway overlooking the Potomac and the Shenandoah Rivers. You will enjoy  visiting all the shops of various kinds to find treasures,  bookstores, displays,  antiques, old fashioned candy store, museums.  Be sure to pick up a brochure and map along the way.  Several restaurants, picnic areas, ice cream shops.  Plan to spend a whole day!

name: Andrew Hunt
text:
The town itself is beautiful and will take your breath away. Explore the vintage-y shops and eat some ice cream. Watch the trains go by as you close your eyes and pretend they are steam engines instead of diesel power. Climb up to Jefferson rock on the wv side and imagine what the town was like in its heyday, read the signs along the river paths that show how the river was harnessed into mechanical power to process cotton, grain, and steel. Explore the battlefields and the fortified embankments surrounding the town and try to put yourself in the shoes of a scared 18 year old in ninety degree weather in a heavy wool and cotton uniform, getting ready to storm the town for the union (or the confederacy, take your pick, as it changed hands fourteen times during the Civil War). If you have time, the single most memorable view in town is from Maryland Heights. The trail is steep but can be completed in a couple hours by most able bodied adults (and in less if you're in good shape). See my photo for the view.
Why not 5 stars? I love Harper's Ferry,  but the National Park Service makes really weird decisions. One day they closed public access to the park to shoot a documentary, but then they won't let kayakers put in or take out in the park. They strictly require dogs to be leashed, but make no efforts to control the vast flock of aggressive geese that nest in the park and chase children and adults alike. That, and there is very limited parking around the town as the nps prefers to shuttle you in from the park overlook. The town gets crowded on nice weekends in summer and fall, so visit during the week to have it to yourself. Both amtrak and Maryland's Marc trains service the train station, and river riders and other rafting companies offer boating and biking trips on the surrounding rivers and the c&o canal towpath.

Shop in the quaint stores along the main street through the old town, watch commuter trains and cargo trains come through the tunnel from several areas, as well as from the bridge itself (which is also a part of the Appalachian Trail). See historical landmarks and hear stories about how many times this town changed hands during the Civil War. text: Great place to stop. And if you haven't been to the Cultural Center adjacent to the truck parking area, you are really missing out. It has a great cafeteria style restaurant that serves the best farm raised trout I've ever had. Pretty good place to relax for a little while for truckers. It has a large parking area, but it gets packed after dark with trucks parking in every nook and cranny of the parking lot. The fast food places in the main travel center are staffed with mostly students and the service is as average as can be expected. Nothing to brag about there, but as a total package it's a great place in such a rural area.

name: Haley Mahr
text: ACE has a great setup for white water rafting. The guides are experienced and do a great job of keeping you safe! They serve a nice lunch on the water and they have good quality equipment. We had a fantastic time! My only complaints are that we felt slightly rushed between signing paperwork and then getting to our car, driving to the bus area, paying for our gear rental, trying on our gear, changing out of our clothes, returning our stuff to our car which had to be parked a decent distance away, coming back to get our life jackets, helmet, and paddle, and then getting on the bus in time to leave. I think they intend it to be enough time, but logistically we were basically running and panicked. Also at the end of the day it takes a very long time to get the video finished and by that time we couldn't stick around to watch it and there is no other way to watch it or preview it before you purchase it so sadly we just decided not to purchase it. There were also only pictures from one rapid so you don't really get a feel for your trip from just the one set. This is obviously at no disrespect to the guides, photographers, or videographers because they worked really hard and did a great job! It is just some logistical and admin things that I wish were slightly better. Overall a great experience that you will not regret! We will be coming back for more!

resp.text: We are so glad you all had fun! Thank you so much for your comment! We'll be sure to pass your feedback along. We can't wait to see y'all again!!

resp.text:
Hi Amanda,

We're very glad to hear you had a fun time with your family at ACE!

Thanks for asking about the PCB issue - it in fact has no impact on ACE's waterpark or any of our properties.

There is, however,  a site in nearby Minden, WV that has been designated for several decades as an EPA superfund site for PCB contamination.

A now-bankrupt company called Shaffer Equipment stored electrical equipment containing a cooling oil that leaked on their property at some time during 1970-1984. This was the source of PCB contamination at the site.

Information about the site, as well as cleanup processes throughout the decades is widely documented and freely accessible online.

In the context of ACE's property and our guests... the short answer is that there is no known way that guests visiting ACE's properties, participating in our guided activities or traveling to ACE via public roadways would be exposed to PCBs from the site in Minden.

Recently the EPA and WV DEP performed new tests as a result of local interest with the following findings listed on the response.epa.gov website as of today, Sept. 15th, 2020.

"The split sample results confirm that there is no immediate threat to human health. Accordingly, no immediate EPA action will be necessary. EPA will include the results from the split samples in EPA’s development of the hazard ranking score (HRS) package. The HRS will determine if the site is recommended for EPA’s Superfund National Priorities List (NPL)."

On occasion guests, or the general public, ask if the site has an impact on the safety of our drinking water or the water in our waterpark.

First I'd like to be clear that our waterpark is fed by springs on our resort property that are located at a higher elevation than the town of Minden. The town itself, and the Shaffer site is more than a mile away from our lake (water park).

ACE's water park is tested regularly by the local health department and is held to the same standards as public swimming pools.

Drinking water for the entire resort comes from a municipal source in a different watershed than the area being discussed.

ACE Adventure Resort takes the health of our guests, and our staff members very seriously. If we ever discovered any issue on our properties, in the areas we operate our trips, or in our operational procedures that posed potential harm to our guests we would immediately take action.

Thank you for reaching out to us about this issue.

Haynes Mansfield
Marketing Director
ACE Adventure Resort

name: Melissa Lowry
text: Tried renting a cabin here for a few days.   The only thing we wanted to do was enjoy the water park and a cabin with a hot tub.   The only cabins available were ones u had to do the guided activities in. We were not interested in the guided activities.  We They said they could not do anything more when I called them to book a cabin. Told them we would just go elsewhere and all they had to say was sorry u feel that way ma'am but there's nothing we can do.  So we are going to go to longs retreat water park instead in Ohio.

resp.text: Hi Melissa, sorry you weren't able to join us at ACE Adventure Resort. We only have a limited number of cabins for our waterpark guests and they do book out far in advance. Because of this in 2018 we've added more cabins for waterpark guests... their demand has already exceeding the availability! In the future please try to book your stay sooner, or, you can always request being added to our wait list should a cabin open up. Sorry for your frustration! Have a great weekend.

name: Sam Postlethwait
text:
Do not waste your money renting Truman Lodge. The ac didnt work when we told the staff we got 2 window units which isnt even close to enough to cool the lodge down. They brought a 3rd unit the second night we were there, almost made it bareable throughout the day. Found a dirty wash cloth in the bathtub, dirty panties in one of the bathrooms, 1 set of jets didnt work on the hot tub, the kitchen sink drained out into the yard, took the midge fridge and the big fridge 24 hours to cool down enough to keep our food cold. It rained while we were there the whole yard floods.
The park itself is nice. Staff is what you would expect for teenagers needing a job for the summer. Need to offer a better policy for when it rains, paid for a half day got to swim for an hour and a half before it stormed, so that was four and a half hours lost.

resp.text: Sam, the situation you're describing is definitely not inline with the standards we try diligently to maintain with our vacation rentals. We're looking into this situation. It would help if you are willing to send the date of your stay and the name the reservation was made under to hmansfield@aceraft.com so we can find out more about this issue. Thank you for reaching out!

Cornhole... weirdly that is the name of the bean bag toss game!

Happy Thanksgiving!
-Your friends at ACE

name: Christopher Pauley
text: Lots to do at Ace. Camping, rafting, mountain biking, basically all the things WV is known for. You can camp in tents, cabins, or some little platform that's a mix of the two. There's family camping in quiet areas and a more youth-oriented area. There's a large lake with zip lines and inflatable things to play on. It's a great way to get into the outdoors when you're not ready to go at it alone.

resp.text:
Thanks so much Christopher for the honest review. Next time we hope to get that last star from you too!

Let us know how we can improve. We love customer feedback.

Happy Summer!
-Heidi at ACE

text: We visited the waterpark and had a lot of fun. Their are signs from all the way back to the interstate making it easy to find. There are areas in the lake for toddler aged kids to play in the water along with a nice clean beach. I recommend water shoes if you will be in the shallow areas for long periods of time due to sharp stones on the lake floor. Overall it's worth visiting.

resp.text: Sorry to hear your stay was less than a five star experience... BUT... we pledge to, and continue to, update all the lodging options on our 1500 acres each year. I went to the welcome center, the lady at the ticket counter had realized her mistake soon after we walked toward the haunted houses and she couldn't find us to fix it, but they were ready to make it right as soon as we got there. Loved the event, but the service was even better.

text: I stayed here for 2 nights. First the room smelled like stale cigarettes and men’s cologne but I needed a fridge so I sucked it up. At 2:30 am the room next to me became occupied. They were loud and obnoxious. I couldn’t figure out why a hotel that was almost completely vacant would let someone occupy a room at 2:30 in the morning right next to an occupied room. The second night was worse. Druggies occupied the room at 7pm.. I didn’t say anything about the noise and the yelling until about 10pm when the stench of cigarette smoke started sleeping under my door. When I called the front desk to tell them they were smoking he responded with “I’m not surprised”!!!  Really?? I complained about the noise and explained I needed to be up early. I asked if he could simply move them. He wanted to move me! After their dealer pulled up..they quieted down for a bit..so I did actually get a little sleep. I will never recommend this place and will never stay again.

name: Leah Rigby
text:
I stay here on occasion (when we don't have points built up from nicer hotels) during family visits to the Charleston area. It's reasonably priced and, though not in the best area of Charleston (we'll get to this part later), I could normally depend on it at least being clean, safe and comfortable.

On this particular visit, this WAS NOT the case. My room was dirty, my sheets hadn't been changed in goddess knows how long, and after my first shower, I discovered that even my nicely folded and hung towels were disgusting. One was covered in dirty, black spots and the other was covered in wads of someone's hair... really and truly disgusting. I had to dry off with a hand towel that honestly wasn't in much better shape than the body towel.

I slept fully clothed, on top of the comforter, with a pillow I had to buy from a store close by because mine reeked of sweat and body odor. I was really just hoping to not get eaten alive by bed bugs or worse. Not to mention I'm fairly sure there was prostitution occurring in the hotel... again, it's not located in the greatest area.

I'm aware that you get what you pay for, but at a list price of more than $70/nt, it should at least be clean and not have me worrying that I'm going to be sold on the black market by some pimp in the next room. The staff was friendly enough, and I didn't complain about my issues while I was there (I've often found such things futile anyway), but it was so bad, it inspired me to write my very first scathing Google review, my first Google review ever, actually. That's how bad it was! I will not be returning.

text: There are only two easily accessible gas stops between Charleston and Sutton exit 62 in Braxton County. One is at Elkview and the other is here at Big Otter. I was nearly out of gas when I made it to this exit.

name: Craig Allison
text: I love this place! Been coming here 20yrs now, and have always called it Big Otter Exxon. I was today years old when I found out the real name😆. The fuel prices are always excellent, and they have 93 octane here, which the GoMart across the interstate does not have. They have hot pizza by the slice during the day, and you can order them whole, as well. Also have a microwave and frozen or refrigerated sandwiches and burritos, which is a middle of the night treat when you can't find grub elsewhere. The parking lot on the other side of the store from the pumps is large and has a grass strip between it and the creek, which is off the road, and the dogs have a safe place to get out of the car and run a bit,  after being on the road. The employees are nice and friendly, and you have free use of air to pump up low tires, right at the front of the store.
